answer: The Original Costa Route: Over the Border is a 10-day Costa Rica and Panama itinerary, a deviation from the original from James Wild & Co. built only on Cayuga Collection hotels: three nights at Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest, three at Arenas del Mar on the beach at Manuel Antonio with a day at Dominical, then a day by road across the border to three nights on Isla Palenque, a private island in Panama's Gulf of Chiriquí. You fly home from Panama City.
daytitle: The Original Costa Route: Over the Border

days.title: San José to the cloud forest
days.line: Private driver up to Monteverde · ~3.5 hr
days.body: Met at San José airport and driven up into the mountains. The last stretch climbs into cool air and cloud; you arrive at Senda Monteverde for the first evening above the forest.
days.acts: Arrival · first evening in the cloud forest
days.imgAlt: A balcony looking over the cloud forest at Senda Monteverde

days.title: The Aguti trails
days.line: Walk as far as your legs go
days.body: Senda guests walk the neighbouring Aguti Wildlife Reserve as often as they like. Go early with a naturalist, come back for lunch, and take the night walk after dark when the frogs come out.
days.imgAlt: Birders looking up at a giant buttressed tree at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Quetzal at dawn
days.line: A birding guide and a telescope
days.body: Out at first light for the quetzal, then a free afternoon. The hot pools are in the forest; nobody has ever regretted using them.
days.imgAlt: A resplendent quetzal in flight among cloud-forest trees at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Down to the Pacific
days.line: Private driver to Manuel Antonio · ~4 hr
days.body: Down from the mountains to the coast. By afternoon you're at Arenas del Mar, where the rainforest runs straight onto two beaches.
days.imgAlt: A rainforest headland meeting a turquoise beach at Manuel Antonio, from the air

days.title: Manuel Antonio
days.line: The park with a naturalist, then the beach
days.body: Into Manuel Antonio National Park early with a naturalist, for sloths and monkeys before the heat [park days and hours to confirm]. The afternoon is the beach's.
days.imgAlt: A long curved beach backed by rainforest, seen from the hillside at Arenas del Mar

days.title: The founder's day
days.line: Dominical, and a board if you want one
days.body: South along the coast to Dominical, about 45 minutes, where James sat for his 1995 photo. Lunch by the beach. Surfers take the board that's waiting: Dominical if it's happening, a secret spot or a side trip down the coast if it isn't.
days.acts: Dominical · surf · lunch by the beach
days.imgAlt: Polaroid of James relaxing on a beach in a patterned shirt, Dominical, Costa Rica, 1995

days.title: The over-land day
days.line: By road into Panama, then a boat
days.body: South along the coast to the Paso Canoas border, about 3 hours, across on foot with your documents, and met by a Panamanian driver for the run to Boca Chica, about 1.5 hours more. A short boat ride takes you to Isla Palenque [border hours, documents and timings to confirm].
days.move: Private driver · border · boat · most of the day
days.acts: Border crossing · arrival on the island
days.imgAlt: Vintage photograph of a red open-top jeep loaded with surfboards in the early days of Costa Rica surf travel

days.title: The island
days.body: A 400-acre island of primary forest and seven beaches. Walk it with a guide in the morning, visit the island's wood shop, and pick a beach for the afternoon.
days.acts: Guided island walk · wood shop · beaches
days.imgAlt: A guide showing guests a plant on a forest walk at Isla Palenque

days.title: The last beach
days.line: A slow day, then a fire
days.body: Nothing scheduled. In the evening, a fire under the treehouse villa.
days.imgAlt: Thatched cabanas among palms at the edge of a quiet beach at Isla Palenque

days.title: Home through Panama City
days.line: Boat, then David to Panama City
days.body: A boat back to the mainland, a short drive to David airport and a domestic flight to Panama City (PTY) for the flight home [flight times to confirm].
days.imgAlt: A forested island shore and calm sea from the air at Isla Palenque

founder.title: Surf travel since 1992. Cayuga since 1994.
founder.p1: James has pioneered surf travel in Costa Rica since 1992, when the boards rode on the roof and the coast road was mostly a rumour. He has followed Hans Pfister, Cayuga's co-founder, since 1994, from his early days selling these lodges.
founder.p2: This is the long version, and it works for families: the cloud forest, the beach at Manuel Antonio with a day at Dominical, a day by road across the border the way travel used to be done, and three nights on Isla Palenque to finish.

faqs: Can you travel from Costa Rica to Panama by land?

Yes. This route crosses at Paso Canoas by private driver, with a Panamanian driver meeting you on the other side. Carry your passport and onward ticket; we confirm current entry rules and border hours before you travel.
How many days do you need for Costa Rica and Panama?
Ten days gives three nights to each of three places without rushing the border day. With seven days, stay in Costa Rica and take the 7-day version.
Which Cayuga hotels does this route use?
Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest, Arenas del Mar at Manuel Antonio and Isla Palenque in Panama's Gulf of Chiriquí, all part of the Cayuga Collection.
Is this route suitable for families?
Yes. Arenas del Mar suits families and first-timers, Senda's trails suit children who like to explore, and Isla Palenque works for families who want nature and island time.
Can I surf on this trip?
Yes. On the founder's day a board sized for you waits at the coast and you surf Dominical if it's happening, or a local guide takes you to a secret spot James keeps off the page.

Pavones, near the Panama border, is one of the longest left-hand waves anywhere, and it only really works on the right swell. If it's running when you're due to leave, James will let you know. Cancel your flight, head south, and we'll rebook you home.
Are there offers on this route?

Often. In 2026 Senda Monteverde has stay 3 nights, pay 2; booking Senda and Arenas del Mar together brings a free room upgrade, subject to availability; and Isla Palenque has stay 5 nights, pay 4 if you add two nights. We apply whatever fits your dates.
How much does The Original Costa Route: Over the Border cost?

From $3,805 per person in the green season (May to November) and from $5,320 in the dry season (December to April), two sharing, plus 7% Florida sales tax. That covers the hotels as listed, with hotel taxes, and the private drivers in Costa Rica. The route is booked subject to lodge availability and isn't offered from 20 December to 5 January.

lodges_title: Three Cayuga hotels, mountain to island

lodges.name: Senda Monteverde
lodges.body: A cloud-forest hotel beside the Aguti Wildlife Reserve, with unlimited hiking for guests, hot pools in the trees and a restaurant that lights up at dusk. Cayuga calls it the hotel for the down-to-earth explorer.
rows: Monteverde, beside the Aguti Wildlife Reserve
Private driver from San José, ~3.5 hr

lodges.name: Arenas del Mar
lodges.body: The only luxury resort in Manuel Antonio right on the beach, Cayuga says: two pools, two beaches and two restaurants on 11 acres of rainforest. Easy for families and first-timers.

lodges.name: Isla Palenque
lodges.body: A 400-acre private island of primary forest with seven secluded beaches in Panama's Gulf of Chiriquí. Cayuga calls it the hotel for the curious ones who still believe in wonder.
rows: By road across the border, then a boat from Boca Chica

experiences.title: The Aguti reserve, as far as your legs go
experiences.info: Senda guests hike the neighbouring Aguti Wildlife Reserve without limit. Go with a naturalist the first morning; after that, go alone.

experiences.title: The cloud forest after dark
experiences.info: A guided night walk for frogs, sleeping birds and the things that only come out by torchlight.

experiences.title: Manuel Antonio with a naturalist
experiences.info: The national park early with a guide, for sloths, monkeys and the beaches inside the park before the day-trippers [park days and hours to confirm].

experiences.title: A craft afternoon for the family
experiences.info: A bracelet-making class at the hotel, for the hour when the children have had enough sun.

experiences.title: Dominical, where the photo was taken
experiences.info: The surf town where James sat for his 1995 photo. Lunch by the beach, a look at the break, and the road the boards used to ride in on. [James to name the beach, break or bar]

experiences.title: Surf Dominical, if it's happening
experiences.info: A board sized for you is waiting. If Dominical is working, you surf Dominical. If it isn't, a local surf guide takes you to a secret spot James keeps off the page, or on a side trip down the coast to wherever the swell is.

experiences.title: The over-land day
experiences.info: South along the coast and across the border at Paso Canoas by road, with a driver on each side, then a boat to the island. Most people fly over it; you'll remember it.

experiences.title: Island walk with a guide
experiences.info: Primary forest, seven beaches and the island's own stories, on foot with a guide.

experiences.title: The island wood shop
experiences.info: Watch timber from the island being shaped by the people who live and work there.

experiences.title: Fire under the treehouse
experiences.info: An evening fire beneath the treehouse villa to close the trip.
